item.content:encoded:
Concrete Driveways in Melbourne

Need a new concrete driveway in Melbourne or the old one replaced? We install plain, exposed aggregate, coloured and decorative concrete driveways across Melbourne — properly prepped, reinforced and finished to last. Book a free on-site quote and we'll give you a fixed price before any work starts.

Whatever look you're after, here's what we lay most

DRIVEWAY FINISHES WE DO:

Plain concrete driveways

The durable, cost-effective standard. Clean, hard-wearing, low maintenance.

Exposed aggregate

Stone revealed in the surface for a textured, non-slip, high-end finish.

Coloured & stencil

Colour through the mix or stencilled patterns for kerb appeal.

Reinforced & heavy-duty

Extra steel and thickness for caravans, boats or steep access.

HOW WE BUILD A DRIVEWAY THAT LASTS

  1. Site prep & excavation — clear the area, set levels, dig to the right depth.
  2. Base & compaction — crushed rock base, properly compacted so nothing shifts later.
  3. Formwork & steel — form the edges, lay reinforcing mesh or bar sized to the load.
  4. Pour & finish — pour, screed level, and apply your chosen finish (broom, exposed, coloured).'
  5. Joints & curing — cut expansion joints to control cracking, then cure properly before use.
Contact us
  • ABN: 24 280 418 757
  • Melbourne CBD
  • Mon-Fri 9:00AM - 5:00PM

Exposed Aggregate Concrete in Melbourne

Exposed aggregate is the premium concrete finish that reveals the stone in the mix for a textured, non-slip surface with serious kerb appeal. We lay exposed aggregate driveways, paths, patios and pool surrounds across Melbourne — colour-matched to your home and sealed to last. Book a free on-site quote and we'll give you a fixed price before any work starts.

WHAT IS EXPOSED AGGREGATE?

Exposed aggregate is concrete where the top layer of cement is washed back before it fully sets, exposing the decorative stones (the "aggregate") underneath. Instead of a flat grey surface you get a natural, pebbled texture. That texture is what makes it both good-looking and grippy underfoot — which is why it's a favourite for driveways and around pools.

Driveways

The most popular use; hard-wearing with standout kerb appeal.

Paths and Pathways

Non-slip surface for side access and garden paths.

Patios & Alfresco

Textured entertaining areas that tie into the garden.

Pool Surrounds

The non-slip finish makes it a common choice around pools.

STONE & COLOUR OPTIONS

Exposed aggregate isn't one look — the stone and mix change the whole result. Options range from natural river pebbles to crushed granite and quartz, in tones from pale sandstone through to charcoal. We'll help you match the aggregate to your home's colours at the quote stage, and you can see samples before you commit.

WHY CHOOSE EXPOSED AGGREGATE

  • Non-slip — the textured surface gives grip, wet or dry — ideal for slopes and pools.
  • Durable — as tough as standard concrete, with decades of life when sealed and maintained.
  • Kerb appeal — a higher-end look that lifts the front of a home and adds value.
  • Low maintenance — an occasional reseal and a hose-down is most of the upkeep.

LOOKING AFTER YOUR EXPOSED AGGREGATE

Exposed aggregate is low-maintenance but not no-maintenance. A rinse or gentle wash keeps it clean, and resealing every few years protects the surface and keeps the colour rich. We'll tell you what your specific finish needs and when.

HOW WE LAY EXPOSED AGGREGATE

Getting exposed aggregate right is about timing — expose too early and stones dislodge, too late and they won't show. Our process:

  1. Base & formwork — same solid prep as any pour: compacted base, formed edges, reinforcing.
  2. Pour & place aggregate — either mixed through the concrete or seeded onto the surface.
  3. Wash back at the right moment — expose the stone once the concrete has set to the correct point.
  4. Clean & cure — rinse off residue, then cure properly.
  5. Seal — a sealer locks in the colour, protects the surface and brings out the stone.

WHAT DOES EXPOSED AGGREGATE COST IN MELBOURNE?

Exposed aggregate costs more than plain concrete — the decorative stone, the extra labour to expose it, and sealing all add to the price. Exactly how much depends on the area, the aggregate you choose and site access. We give a free on-site fixed-price quote so you know the real number before committing.

Get a free fixed-price quote →

AREAS WE SERVICE

We lay exposed aggregate across Melbourne, including Werribee, Point Cook, Tarneit, Hoppers Crossing, Melton, Craigieburn, Cranbourne, Berwick, Pakenham and Frankston.

FAQ

How much more does exposed aggregate cost than plain concrete?

It’s a premium finish, so it costs more than plain concrete — the decorative stone, the extra labour to expose it and the sealing all add up. The gap depends on the aggregate and the area; we give a free on-site quote with the exact figure. 

Is exposed aggregate slippery?

The opposite — the exposed stone creates a textured, non-slip surface, which is exactly why it’s popular for driveways, slopes and around pools.

Does exposed aggregate need sealing? (

Yes. Sealing protects the surface, brings out the colour of the stone and makes cleaning easier. It’s typically resealed every few years depending on wear and exposure.

How long does exposed aggregate last?

It’s as durable as standard concrete — decades of life when it’s laid on a proper base and kept sealed. Good prep and maintenance are what determine longevity.

Can you lay exposed aggregate over an existing driveway?

It depends on the condition of the existing slab. In most cases a fresh pour on a properly prepared base gives the best, longest-lasting result — we’ll assess and advise at the on-site quote.

What colours and stones can I choose?

A wide range — from pale river pebbles to charcoal granite and quartz. We help match the aggregate to your home’s colours and show you samples before you decide.

Concreters in Werribee

Looking for concreters in Werribee? We pour driveways, exposed aggregate, slabs, paths and patios right across Werribee and the wider Wyndham area — properly based, reinforced and finished to last. With new homes going up across the western growth corridor, we do a lot of driveway and slab work locally. Book a free on-site quote and we'll give you a fixed price before any work starts.

Contact us - 0480 804 014

SOME OF THE LOCAL WORK WE'VE DONE IN WERRIBEE:

Our Concreting Services in Werribee

Everything we do, available across Werribee:

  • Concrete driveways — new driveways, replacements and crossovers for Werribee homes. 
  • Exposed aggregate — the premium non-slip finish, popular on newer Werribee builds. 
  • Concrete slabs  — shed, garage and floor slabs. 
  • Paths & pathways — side access and garden paths.
  • Patios & alfresco — outdoor entertaining areas. 

Concreting Across Werribee & Wyndham

Werribee sits in the City of Wyndham, one of Melbourne's fastest-growing areas — which means a lot of new homes needing driveways, slabs and outdoor areas. A couple of local things worth knowing: a new vehicle crossover (the bit from the road to your property) generally needs approval from Wyndham City Council, and the newer estates often have specific requirements — we sort that out as part of the job so you're not chasing council yourself.

AREAS WE COVER AROUND WERRIBEE

We service Werribee and the surrounding Wyndham suburbs, including Werribee South, Wyndham Vale, Hoppers Crossing, Point Cook, Tarneit and Truganina.

WHY WERRIBEE CUSTOMERS CHOOSE US

benefit 1

Local, on-site fixed-price quotes — we come to you in Werribee and price the job on site.

benefit 2

Groundwork done properly — compacted base and correct reinforcement, not a fast pour.

benefit 3

Licensed & insured

Benefit 4

Workmanship guarantee

Local Testimonial

"They did our driveway and did a fantastic job with the whole thing — sorted out all the details and the quote easily, no fuss. Couldn't be happier." Sasha C - Werribee

GET A FREE WERRIBEE CONCRETING QUOTE

Tell us about the job and we'll book an on-site measure and give you a fixed price. Pricing depends on size, finish and access — the only accurate number is an on-site quote.

Get Free Quote Now

FAQ

Do you service Werribee?

Yes — Werribee is one of our core areas. We cover Werribee and the surrounding Wyndham suburbs for driveways, slabs, exposed aggregate, paths and patios.

Do I need council approval for a driveway crossover in Werribee?

A new vehicle crossover onto the road generally needs approval from Wyndham City Council; a driveway on your own property often doesn’t. We’ll point you to the right requirements before we start.

How much does a concrete driveway cost in Werribee?


It depends on size, finish and access — plain concrete is the most affordable, exposed aggregate and decorative finishes cost more. We give a free on-site fixed-price quote.

item.content:encoded:
Concreters in Point Cook

Point Cook is one of Melbourne's fastest-growing suburbs, and its new estates mean a steady stream of homes needing everything from fresh driveways to full outdoor areas. We handle the concreting side — new driveways and crossovers, exposed aggregate, slabs, paths and patios — built on a properly compacted base so they last. Whether you're finishing a new build in Sanctuary Lakes or replacing a tired driveway in an older street, we'll come out, measure the job and give you a fixed price before any work starts.

Contact us - 0480 804 014

Our Work in Point Cook:

Our Concreting Services in Point Cook

Everything we do, available across Point:

  • Concrete driveways — new driveways, replacements and crossovers for Werribee homes. 
  • Exposed aggregate — the premium non-slip finish, popular on newer Werribee builds.

CONCRETING FOR POINT COOK'S NEW ESTATES

Point Cook is one of Melbourne's fastest-growing suburbs, built around large master-planned estates like Sanctuary Lakes, Saltwater Coast, Alamanda and Boardwalk. That means a lot of brand-new homes needing driveways, slabs and outdoor areas from scratch — and newer builds where owners want a finish that lifts the look, which is why exposed aggregate and coloured concrete are popular around here. Being close to Port Phillip Bay, we also see plenty of outdoor entertaining and pool-side work. Like the rest of the area, Point Cook sits in the City of Wyndham, so a new vehicle crossover generally needs council approval — we sort that as part of the job.

We service Point Cook and the surrounding areas, including Sanctuary Lakes, Saltwater Coast, Williams Landing, Laverton and Seabrook.

What Wyndham Council Actually Requires for a Vehicle Crossing (2026)

The short answer

Need a new concrete driveway in Melbourne or the old one replaced? We install plain, exposed aggregate, coloured and decorative concrete driveways across Melbourne — properly prepped, reinforced and finished to last. Book a free on-site quote and we'll give you a fixed price before any work starts.

Whatever look you're after, here's what we lay most

DRIVEWAY FINISHES WE DO:

Plain concrete driveways

The durable, cost-effective standard. Clean, hard-wearing, low maintenance.

Exposed aggregate

Stone revealed in the surface for a textured, non-slip, high-end finish.

Coloured & stencil

Colour through the mix or stencilled patterns for kerb appeal.

Reinforced & heavy-duty

Extra steel and thickness for caravans, boats or steep access.

HOW WE BUILD A DRIVEWAY THAT LASTS

  1. Site prep & excavation — clear the area, set levels, dig to the right depth.
  2. Base & compaction — crushed rock base, properly compacted so nothing shifts later.
  3. Formwork & steel — form the edges, lay reinforcing mesh or bar sized to the load.
  4. Pour & finish — pour, screed level, and apply your chosen finish (broom, exposed, coloured).'
  5. Joints & curing — cut expansion joints to control cracking, then cure properly before use.
Get Your Free Quote Today

WHY MELBOURNE HOMEOWNERS CHOOSE US

  • On-site fixed-price quotes — we measure before we price, so the number doesn't move.
  • Licensed & insured
  • Workmanship guarantee
  • Local across Melbourne — from the western suburbs to the southeast, one call.

AREAS WE SERVICE

We pour concrete driveways across Melbourne, including Werribee, Point Cook, Tarneit, Hoppers Crossing, Melton, Craigieburn, Cranbourne, Berwick, Pakenham and Frankston.

WHAT DOES A CONCRETE DRIVEWAY COST IN MELBOURNE?

Price comes down to size, finish, site access and whether an old driveway needs removing — plain concrete sits at the lower end, exposed aggregate and decorative finishes cost more. The only accurate number is an on-site measure, which we do free.

FAQ

How much does a concrete driveway cost in Melbourne?

It depends on size, finish and site access. Plain concrete is the most affordable; exposed aggregate and coloured finishes cost more. We give a free on-site fixed-price quote so you know the real number upfront.

How thick should a concrete driveway be?

A standard residential driveway is around 100mm thick with reinforcing mesh. For heavier vehicles like caravans or trucks, we increase the thickness and steel to suit the load.

How long before I can drive on a new concrete driveway?

It’s usually walk-on ready in 24–48 hours and safe for vehicles after about 7 days. Concrete reaches full strength at around 28 days, and cold or wet weather slows curing.

Do I need council approval for a driveway or crossover?

A new vehicle crossover onto the road usually needs council approval; a driveway on your own property often doesn’t. We’ll point you to your council’s requirements before we start.

How long does a concrete driveway last?

A properly laid and cured concrete driveway commonly lasts 30–40 years or more with minimal maintenance — which is why the base prep matters so much.

Do you remove the old driveway?

Yes — we handle demolition and removal of the existing driveway before the new pour. We’ll confirm whether that’s included or quoted separately at the on-site measure.

Concreters in Werribee

From new estates to established homes, we install and replace concrete driveways, crossovers, exposed aggregate, slabs, paths and patios throughout Werribee, with proper site preparation, reinforcement and fixed-price quotes.

Get Your FREE Quote Today Call us - 03 4427 9541

Local Work Completed

Plain Concrete Backyard Slab in Werribee

Concrete Courtyard and Side-Access Area

Large Outdoor Concrete Slab in Werribee

Concrete Work Built for Werribee Conditions

Concrete work in Werribee needs to be planned around the condition of the ground, the existing property levels and the way water moves across the site. Before quoting, we inspect the area so the excavation, base preparation, reinforcement, concrete finish, drainage falls and control joints suit the actual driveway, path, patio or slab.

Ground Conditions and Base Preparation

Ground conditions can vary between Werribee properties. Established blocks may contain clay-based natural ground, while newer homes can have disturbed soil or areas of fill left from construction. Soft or unsuitable material needs to be identified before concrete is poured rather than being covered over.

Where required, the area is excavated and prepared with a properly compacted base before formwork and reinforcement are installed. Correct preparation is particularly important beneath driveways, garage approaches and slabs that will regularly carry vehicles or other heavy loads.

Drainage and Finished Concrete Levels

The finished level of the concrete is just as important as the selected colour or surface finish. The slab needs to be set out so water moves away from the home, garage and other structures instead of collecting along walls, fences or slab edges.

Existing garage floors, door thresholds, paths, drainage points, landscaping and neighbouring surfaces all need to be considered when setting the height and fall of a new driveway, patio or side path.

Control Joints and Crack Management

Concrete naturally contracts as it cures and can continue to move with changes in temperature and ground moisture. Reinforcement helps hold the slab together, but it does not make concrete completely crack-proof.

Control joints provide planned locations for normal shrinkage movement. They are commonly positioned around internal corners, changes in slab width, drainage points, garage entrances and connections between new and existing concrete.

New Estates and Established Werribee Homes

Newer Werribee homes often require a driveway to connect the garage slab with a crossover installed as part of the estate. The driveway levels also need to work with the front path, landscaping, drainage and finished garage height.

Established Werribee homes can require a different approach. Replacing an older driveway may involve removing cracked concrete, checking the material beneath it, matching existing garage and footpath levels and correcting drainage issues before the replacement concrete is poured.

AREAS WE COVER AROUND WERRIBEE

We service Werribee and the surrounding Wyndham suburbs, including Werribee South, Wyndham Vale, Hoppers Crossing, Point Cook, Tarneit and Truganina.

WHY WERRIBEE CUSTOMERS CHOOSE US

Fixed-Price On-Site Quotes in Werribee

Local, on-site fixed-price quotes — we come to you in Werribee and price the job on site.

Proper Base Preparation and Reinforcement

Groundwork done properly — compacted base and correct reinforcement, not a fast pour.

Insured Concreters

Licensed & insured

Workmanship You Can Rely On

Workmanship guarantee

Local Testimonial

"They did our driveway and did a fantastic job with the whole thing — sorted out all the details and the quote easily, no fuss. Couldn't be happier." Sasha C - Werribee

GET A FREE WERRIBEE CONCRETING QUOTE

Tell us about the job and we'll book an on-site measure and give you a fixed price. Pricing depends on size, finish and access — the only accurate number is an on-site quote.

Get Free Quote Now

FAQ

Do you service Werribee?

Yes — Werribee is one of our core areas. We cover Werribee and the surrounding Wyndham suburbs for driveways, slabs, exposed aggregate, paths and patios.

Do I need council approval for a driveway crossover in Werribee?

A new vehicle crossover onto the road generally needs approval from Wyndham City Council; a driveway on your own property often doesn’t. We’ll point you to the right requirements before we start. Check out our Guide

How much does a concrete driveway cost in Werribee?


It depends on size, finish and access — plain concrete is the most affordable, exposed aggregate and decorative finishes cost more. We give a free on-site fixed-price quote.

Concreters Hoppers Crossing

Hoppers Crossing is one of the oldest suburbs in Wyndham — and unlike the new estates around it, it's fully built out. Most homes here went up between the 1970s and 1990s, which means the concrete is doing the same. Original driveways, paths and slabs from that era are now 30 to 50 years old, cracking, lifting and past their use-by date. We handle both sides of that: replacing tired old concrete on established Hoppers Crossing homes, and pouring new work for knockdown-rebuilds and extensions. Free on-site, fixed-price quotes.

Get Your FREE Quote Today Call us - 03 4427 9541

Concreting for an established suburb, not a new estate

Aging concrete on 1970s-90s homes

Hoppers Crossing grew fastest between the early 1970s and the 1990s, and it's now fully built out — there's no new estate land left. That changes the concreting work here. Where Tarneit and Point Cook are about pouring driveways on fresh estate lots, Hoppers Crossing is largely about replacing concrete that's reached the end of its life: original driveways that have cracked and lifted, paths that have become trip hazards, and slabs poured to 1980s standards that never handled the reactive clay properly in the first place.

Knockdown-rebuilds and renovations

The other half of the work is the suburb's steady turnover. With no new land, growth comes from knockdown-rebuilds and renovations of the existing stock — which means new driveways, extension slabs and outdoor areas going in as older homes are updated. We cover both: tearing out and replacing tired concrete, and pouring fresh work for a rebuild or an extension.

The same reactive clay — with older concrete on top of it

Hoppers Crossing sits on the same reactive clay that runs under Werribee and the rest of the western plains — flat volcanic ground, classified Class M to Class H under AS 2870, that swells when wet and shrinks when it dries. It's the reason so much of the suburb's original concrete has cracked: a lot of it was poured decades ago on bases that weren't prepared for how much this ground moves.

That's exactly why a like-for-like replacement isn't the answer — repouring a driveway the same way it was done in 1985 just repeats the failure. We rebuild the base properly: a compacted crushed-rock sub-base, reinforcement held at the correct height on bar chairs, adequate slab thickness, control joints placed to let the slab move, and the right falls so water runs off rather than pooling. On this ground, the base is what decides whether the new concrete lasts 5 years or 40.

Concreting services in Hoppers Crossing

We cover the full range for Hoppers Crossing homes, new and old:

  • Driveway replacement and new driveways — tearing out cracked original driveways and repouring on a proper base.
  • Exposed aggregate — a popular upgrade when replacing a tired plain driveway.
  • Coloured and decorative concrete — for homeowners updating the look during a renovation.
  • Shed, garage and extension slabs — for rebuilds and additions.
  • Paths and side access — replacing lifted, cracked paths that have become trip hazards.
  • Patios and alfresco areas — updating outdoor entertaining spaces.

Crossovers on older Hoppers Crossing properties

On established homes, the vehicle crossover — where the driveway meets the road — is often the original one, decades old and cracked. If you're replacing your driveway, it's the natural time to redo the crossover too. It sits on council land, needs Wyndham City Council consent, comes with a fee and a lead time, and has to be plain concrete where there's a footpath. We handle that consent as part of the job so you're not chasing council yourself.

Concreting across Hoppers Crossing and nearby

We're based in Werribee, five minutes away, so we're in Hoppers Crossing regularly for quotes and work. We also service Werribee, Point Cook, Tarneit and the surrounding Wyndham suburbs. For the full range of what we do, see our concreters Melbourne page.

Get Your FREE Quote Today

FAQ

Do you replace old cracked driveways?

Yes — replacement is most of what we do in Hoppers Crossing, given the suburb’s older housing. We break out the old driveway, rebuild the base properly for the reactive clay, and repour so the new one actually lasts rather than cracking again.

Why did my original driveway crack?

Almost always a base problem. Much of Hoppers Crossing’s original concrete was poured decades ago on bases that weren’t built for how much the local reactive clay moves. A like-for-like repour repeats the mistake — the fix is rebuilding the base correctly.

Can you redo my crossover at the same time?

Yes, and it’s the sensible time to do it. If your driveway’s being replaced, redoing the aging crossover in the same job saves a second setup. It needs Wyndham Council consent, which we handle.

How much does a new driveway cost in Hoppers Crossing?

It depends on size, finish, and whether the old driveway needs removing first. Removal and base rebuild are part of the price on a replacement. We give a fixed on-site quote after measuring.

Aging concrete on 1970s-90s homes

Hoppers Crossing grew fastest between the early 1970s and the 1990s, and it's now fully built out — there's no new estate land left. That changes the concreting work here. Where Tarneit and Point Cook are about pouring driveways on fresh estate lots, Hoppers Crossing is largely about replacing concrete that's reached the end of its life: original driveways that have cracked and lifted, paths that have become trip hazards, and slabs poured to 1980s standards that never handled the reactive clay properly in the first place.

Knockdown-rebuilds and renovations

The other half of the work is the suburb's steady turnover. With no new land, growth comes from knockdown-rebuilds and renovations of the existing stock — which means new driveways, extension slabs and outdoor areas going in as older homes are updated. We cover both: tearing out and replacing tired concrete, and pouring fresh work for a rebuild or an extension.

Hoppers Crossing sits on the same reactive clay that runs under Werribee and the rest of the western plains — flat volcanic ground, classified Class M to Class H under AS 2870, that swells when wet and shrinks when it dries. It's the reason so much of the suburb's original concrete has cracked: a lot of it was poured decades ago on bases that weren't prepared for how much this ground moves.

That's exactly why a like-for-like replacement isn't the answer — repouring a driveway the same way it was done in 1985 just repeats the failure. We rebuild the base properly: a compacted crushed-rock sub-base, reinforcement held at the correct height on bar chairs, adequate slab thickness, control joints placed to let the slab move, and the right falls so water runs off rather than pooling. On this ground, the base is what decides whether the new concrete lasts 5 years or 40.

  • Driveway replacement and new driveways — tearing out cracked original driveways and repouring on a proper base.
  • Exposed aggregate — a popular upgrade when replacing a tired plain driveway.
  • Coloured and decorative concrete — for homeowners updating the look during a renovation.
  • Shed, garage and extension slabs — for rebuilds and additions.
  • Paths and side access — replacing lifted, cracked paths that have become trip hazards.
  • Patios and alfresco areas — updating outdoor entertaining spaces.

item.title: Privacy Policy
item.dc:creator: Admin-iU1Tj
item.content:encoded:
Who we are

Suggested text: Our website address is: http://bestconcretersmelbourne.com.au.

Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Suggested text: Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

Concreters Melbourne Trust for Driveways, Slabs & Exposed Aggregate

Straight, level, properly-cured concrete — driveways, patios, slabs and paths across Melbourne. Free on-site quote, no obligation.

Get Your FREE Quote Today Call 03 4427 9541

Our Services

Whatever the pour, we match you with concreters who do it every week.

Concrete Driveways

New driveways, replacements, crossovers

Exposed Aggregate

The premium textured, non-slip finish with real kerb appeal.

Concrete Slabs

Shed, garage, extension and house slabs fitted properly for your needs

Paths & Pathways

Footpaths, side access, garden paths

Patios & Alfresco

Outdoor entertaining areas

Coloured & Decorative

Coloured, stencil, honed finishes

Concreting Built for Melbourne's West

Werribee, Point Cook, Tarneit and the surrounding growth corridor sit largely on reactive clay — classified Class M to Class H under AS 2870. This ground swells when wet and shrinks when it dries, moving the soil beneath a driveway or slab through the seasons. It's the single biggest reason concrete cracks out here, and it's why prep matters more in the west than almost anywhere in Melbourne.

On new estate lots the ground has usually been compacted by the building trades before the driveway goes in, so the sub-base needs checking rather than assuming. We build for the conditions: a compacted crushed-rock sub-base, reinforcement held at the correct height on bar chairs, adequate slab thickness, control joints placed to let the concrete move, and the right falls so water runs off rather than pooling against the slab. Get those right and the finish — whatever you choose — lasts.

How We Pour Concrete That Lasts

1. On-site assessment. 

We measure the job, check the site access and ground, and give you a fixed price — not a phone guess.

2. Excavation & sub-base. 

We excavate to the right depth and lay a compacted crushed-rock base. On reactive clay this step is what stops future movement.

3. Formwork & reinforcement. 

Boxing set to the correct falls, then steel mesh or bar held up on bar chairs so it sits in the slab, not on the dirt.

4. Pour & finish. 

The right mix and slump for the weather, poured, screeded and finished in your chosen surface — plain, exposed aggregate, coloured or decorative.

5. Curing & sealing. 

Proper curing for strength, and sealing where the finish needs it. Walk-on in 24–48 hours, vehicle-ready around 7 days, full strength at 28.

Why Choose Us

On-site quotes, not phone guesses

We measure the job before we price it, so the number doesn't move on the day.

Built for reactive clay

Most failed concrete is failed base. In Melbourne's west that means building for reactive clay — proper compaction, correct steel height, adequate thickness and the right falls — so the slab handles seasonal ground movement instead of cracking through it.

We handle the council crossover

A new driveway that meets the road needs a council-approved crossover before it's poured. We sort the consent and build it to council spec as part of the job, so you're not chasing paperwork yourself.

Client Testimonials

"They did our driveway and did a fantastic job with the whole thing — sorted out all the details and the quote easily, no fuss. Couldn't be happier." Sasha C - Werribee "They concreted our poolside area and I loved how smooth the finish came out. Fast, clean, and barely a hiccup the whole way through." Raymond -Narre warren ""They did our patio and I was impressed by how seriously they took safety on site, and the quality of the tradesmen. Proper professionals."" Tim - Brighton

Service Areas

We pour across Melbourne. Popular areas:

Werribee · Point Cook · Tarneit · Truganina · Hoppers Crossing ·  Truganina and More

FAQ

How much does a concrete driveway cost in Melbourne?

It depends on size, finish and site access. Plain concrete sits at the lower end, while exposed aggregate and decorative finishes cost more. We’ve broken down concrete driveway costs per square metre in Melbourne in detail, or book a free on-site quote for a fixed price on your job.”

How long before I can drive on new concrete?

Concrete is usually walk-on ready in 24–48 hours and safe for vehicle traffic after about 7 days, reaching full strength around 28 days. Cold or wet weather slows curing.

Do I need a permit for a driveway or crossover?

A new vehicle crossover onto the road usually needs council approval; a driveway on your own property often doesn’t. We can point you to your council’s requirements before we start.

What's the difference between plain and exposed aggregate concrete?

Exposed aggregate reveals the stone in the mix for a textured, non-slip, higher-end look — it costs more but adds kerb appeal and grip.

 

Do you handle removal of the old driveway?

Yes – we take care of the full job, including breaking up and removing your existing driveway before we pour the new one. That covers demolition, hauling away the old concrete, and prepping the base so the new slab goes down on solid, properly compacted ground. We’ll confirm whether removal is included in your quote or priced separately when we come out to measure, so there are no surprises on the day.

Werribee, Point Cook, Tarneit and the surrounding growth corridor sit largely on reactive clay<\/strong> \u2014 classified Class M to Class H under AS 2870. This ground swells when wet and shrinks when it dries, moving the soil beneath a driveway or slab through the seasons. It's the single biggest reason concrete cracks out here, and it's why prep matters more in the west than almost anywhere in Melbourne.<\/p>\n

On new estate lots the ground has usually been compacted by the building trades before the driveway goes in, so the sub-base needs checking rather than assuming. We build for the conditions: a compacted crushed-rock sub-base, reinforcement held at the correct height on bar chairs, adequate slab thickness, control joints placed to let the concrete move, and the right falls so water runs off rather than pooling against the slab. Get those right and the finish \u2014 whatever you choose \u2014 1. On-site assessment.<\/strong> <\/p>

We measure the job, check the site access and ground, and give you a fixed price \u2014 not a phone guess.<\/p>\n

2. Excavation & sub-base.<\/strong> <\/p>

We excavate to the right depth and lay a compacted crushed-rock base. On reactive clay this step is what stops future movement.<\/p>\n

3. Formwork & reinforcement.<\/strong> <\/p>

Boxing set to the correct falls, then steel mesh or bar held up on bar chairs so it sits in the slab, not on the dirt.<\/p>\n

4. Pour & finish.<\/strong> <\/p>

The right mix and slump for the weather, poured, screeded and finished in your chosen surface \u2014 plain, exposed aggregate, coloured or decorative.<\/p>\n

5. Curing & sealing.<\/strong> <\/p>

Proper curing for strength, and sealing where the finish needs it. Walk-on in 24\u201348 hours, vehicle-ready around 7 days, full strength at item.title: Exposed Aggregate
item.dc:creator: Admin-iU1Tj
item.content:encoded:
Exposed Aggregate Concrete in Melbourne​

Exposed aggregate is the premium concrete finish that reveals the stone in the mix for a textured, non-slip surface with serious kerb appeal. We lay exposed aggregate driveways, paths, patios and pool surrounds across Melbourne — colour-matched to your home and sealed to last. Book a free on-site quote and we'll give you a fixed price before any work starts. Concrete in Melbourne​

WHAT IS EXPOSED AGGREGATE?

Exposed aggregate is concrete where the top layer of cement is washed back before it fully sets, exposing the decorative stones (the "aggregate") underneath. Instead of a flat grey surface you get a natural, pebbled texture. That texture is what makes it both good-looking and grippy underfoot — which is why it's a favourite for driveways and around pools.

Driveways

The most popular use; hard-wearing with standout kerb appeal.

Paths and Pathways

Non-slip surface for side access and garden paths.

Patios & Alfresco

Textured entertaining areas that tie into the garden.

Pool Surrounds

The non-slip finish makes it a common choice around pools.

STONE & COLOUR OPTIONS

Exposed aggregate isn't one look — the stone and mix change the whole result. Options range from natural river pebbles to crushed granite and quartz, in tones from pale sandstone through to charcoal. We'll help you match the aggregate to your home's colours at the quote stage, and you can see samples before you commit.

WHY CHOOSE EXPOSED AGGREGATE

  • Non-slip — the textured surface gives grip, wet or dry — ideal for slopes and pools.
  • Durable — as tough as standard concrete, with decades of life when sealed and maintained.
  • Kerb appeal — a higher-end look that lifts the front of a home and adds value.
  • Low maintenance — an occasional reseal and a hose-down is most of the upkeep.

LOOKING AFTER YOUR EXPOSED AGGREGATE

Exposed aggregate is low-maintenance but not no-maintenance. A rinse or gentle wash keeps it clean, and resealing every few years protects the surface and keeps the colour rich. We'll tell you what your specific finish needs and when.

HOW WE LAY EXPOSED AGGREGATE

Getting exposed aggregate right is about timing — expose too early and stones dislodge, too late and they won't show. Our process:

  1. Base & formwork — same solid prep as any pour: compacted base, formed edges, reinforcing.
  2. Pour & place aggregate — either mixed through the concrete or seeded onto the surface.
  3. Wash back at the right moment — expose the stone once the concrete has set to the correct point.
  4. Clean & cure — rinse off residue, then cure properly.
  5. Seal — a sealer locks in the colour, protects the surface and brings out the stone.

WHAT DOES EXPOSED AGGREGATE COST IN MELBOURNE?

Exposed aggregate costs more than plain concrete — the decorative stone, the extra labour to expose it, and sealing all add to the price. Exactly how much depends on the area, the aggregate you choose and site access, and our concrete cost guide sets out the typical per-square-metre gap between plain and exposed finishes. We give a free on-site fixed-price quote so you know the real number before committing.

AREAS WE SERVICE

We lay exposed aggregate across Melbourne, including Werribee, Point Cook, Tarneit, Hoppers Crossing, Truganina and more.

Get your free exposed aggregate quote!

Tell us about the job and we'll book an on-site measure and fixed price.

Get a free fixed-price quote →

FAQ

How much more does exposed aggregate cost than plain concrete?

It’s a premium finish, so it costs more than plain concrete — the decorative stone, the extra labour to expose it and the sealing all add up. The gap depends on the aggregate and the area; we give a free on-site quote with the exact figure. 

Is exposed aggregate slippery?

The opposite — the exposed stone creates a textured, non-slip surface, which is exactly why it’s popular for driveways, slopes and around pools.

Does exposed aggregate need sealing? (

Yes. Sealing protects the surface, brings out the colour of the stone and makes cleaning easier. It’s typically resealed every few years depending on wear and exposure.

How long does exposed aggregate last?

It’s as durable as standard concrete — decades of life when it’s laid on a proper base and kept sealed. Good prep and maintenance are what determine longevity.

Can you lay exposed aggregate over an existing driveway?

It depends on the condition of the existing slab. In most cases a fresh pour on a properly prepared base gives the best, longest-lasting result — we’ll assess and advise at the on-site quote.

What colours and stones can I choose?

A wide range — from pale river pebbles to charcoal granite and quartz. We help match the aggregate to your home’s colours and show you samples before you decide.

item.title: Concrete Slabs in Melbourne
item.dc:creator: Admin-iU1Tj
item.content:encoded:
Concrete Slabs Melbourne

Need a concrete slab for a shed, garage, extension or outdoor floor? We pour properly based, reinforced and level slab-on-ground concrete across Melbourne — the kind that doesn't sink, crack or shift, because the compacted base and steel reinforcement were done right before the pour. Book a free on-site quote and we'll give you a fixed price before any work starts.

What a Concrete Slab is:

A concrete slab is a flat, reinforced layer of concrete poured over a prepared base — the foundation for sheds, garages, floors and outdoor structures. The visible pour is the easy part; the strength and lifespan come from the sub-base, the reinforcing steel, the slab thickness and proper curing. A slab poured on a poorly compacted base cracks and settles no matter how good the concrete mix is, which is why the groundwork matters as much as the pour itself.

Types of Slabs

Shed slabs

— level, durable bases for garden sheds, workshops and storage.

Garage slabs

— reinforced to carry vehicle loads, with the correct fall for drainage.

Patios & Alfresco Slabs

— the structural base beneath an outdoor living area.

Extension & floor slabs

— floor slabs for extensions, granny flats and outdoor rooms, poured to engineering specifications where required.

Why Choose Concrete Slabs

  • Non-slip — the textured surface gives grip, wet or dry — ideal for slopes and pools.
  • Durable — as tough as standard concrete, with decades of life when sealed and maintained.
  • Kerb appeal — a higher-end look that lifts the front of a home and adds value.
  • Low maintenance — an occasional reseal and a hose-down is most of the upkeep.

SLAB THICKNESS & REINFORCEMENT

The right slab is matched to its load, not a generic spec:

  • Standard slabs are typically around 100mm thick with reinforcing steel mesh (commonly SL72).
  • Heavier loads — vehicles, machinery, structures — get increased thickness and heavier reinforcement.
  • Thickened edges (edge beams) or footings are added where the slab carries walls or posts.
  • A compacted crushed-rock base and a vapour barrier (plastic membrane / DPM) sit under the slab to control moisture and movement.
  • Concrete strength is specified in MPa (typically 20–32 MPa) to suit the job.

We size the thickness, mesh and mix at the on-site quote so the slab suits the load.

WHY MELBOURNE CUSTOMERS CHOOSE US

  • On-site fixed-price quotes — we assess the ground and measure before we price.
  • Groundwork done properly — compaction, base, membrane and correctly placed reinforcement, not just a fast pour.
  • Licensed & Insured
  • Workmanship Guarantee

HOW WE POUR A SLAB

  • Site prep & excavation — clear, level and set out the area to the correct depth.
  • Base & compaction — lay and compact a crushed-rock sub-base so the slab sits on solid ground.
  • Membrane & formwork — plastic vapour barrier, then formwork set to the right levels and falls.
  • Reinforcement — reinforcing mesh or bar, sized to the load and positioned within the slab on bar chairs.
  • Pour, screed & cure — pour the concrete, screed dead level, finish, cut control joints and cure properly so it gains strength evenly.

WHAT DOES A CONCRETE SLAB COST IN MELBOURNE?

Slab cost comes down to size, thickness, reinforcement, site access and how much base preparation the ground needs — a simple shed slab on flat, easy ground is very different to a reinforced garage slab on a sloping site. We publish real per-square-metre ranges by job type in our concrete cost guide, then give a free on-site fixed-price quote so you know the real number before committing.

WHY SLABS CRACK & HOW WE PREVENT IT

Fine surface cracking is normal in concrete, but structural cracking almost always traces back to the base or the reinforcement — not the concrete itself. We control it with proper compaction, correctly placed reinforcing steel, control joints (saw cuts) at the right spacing to manage shrinkage, and careful curing so the slab gains strength evenly. Get those right and the slab stays sound for decades.

Areas we Service

We lay exposed aggregate across Melbourne, including Werribee, Point Cook, Tarneit, Hoppers Crossing, Truganina and more.

FAQ

How thick should a concrete slab be?

A standard slab is around 100mm thick with reinforcing mesh. Slabs carrying heavier loads — vehicles, machinery or structures — need more thickness and heavier reinforcement, which we size at the quote.

 

How much does a concrete slab cost in Melbourne?

It depends on size, thickness, reinforcement and base prep. A simple shed slab costs less than a reinforced garage slab on a difficult site. We give a free on-site fixed-price quote with the real figure.

How long before I can build on or use a new slab?

Concrete is usually walk-on ready in 24–48 hours and ready for heavier use after about 7 days, reaching full strength (around its rated MPa) at roughly 28 days. We’ll advise the right timing for your job.

Do I need a permit for a concrete slab?


Small slabs like shed bases often don’t, but slabs for structures, extensions or anything load-bearing usually need a building permit and engineering. We’ll flag what your job requires before we start.

Why do concrete slabs crack?

Most structural cracking traces back to a poorly compacted base or incorrect reinforcement — not the concrete. Proper compaction, reinforcing steel and control joints are what prevent it. Check out our extensive guide for further information.

What goes underneath a concrete slab?

A compacted crushed-rock base and a plastic vapour barrier sit under every slab we pour — the base gives support, the membrane controls moisture rising from the ground.

Do you prepare the ground, or does it need to be cleared first?

Yes, we handle excavation and base prep as part of the job / we quote on a cleared site.

    The right slab is matched to its load, not a generic spec:<\/p>

    • Standard slabs<\/strong> are typically around 100mm thick<\/strong> with reinforcing steel mesh<\/strong> (commonly SL72).<\/li>
    • Heavier loads<\/strong> \u2014 vehicles, machinery, structures \u2014 get increased thickness and heavier reinforcement.<\/li>
    • Thickened edges (edge beams) or footings<\/strong> are added where the slab carries walls or posts.<\/li>
    • A compacted crushed-rock base and a vapour barrier<\/strong> (plastic membrane \/ DPM) sit under the slab to control moisture and movement.<\/li>
    • Concrete strength<\/strong> is specified in MPa (typically 20\u201332 MPa) to suit the job.<\/li><\/ul>

      We size the thickness, mesh and mix at the on-site quote so the slab suits the           Fine surface cracking is normal in concrete, but structural cracking almost always traces back to the base or the reinforcement \u2014 not the concrete itself. item.title: Concrete Paths and Pathways Melbourne
item.dc:creator: Admin-iU1Tj
item.content:encoded:
Concrete Paths and Pathways Melbourne

Need a concrete path down the side of the house, through the garden or up to the front door? We lay level, non-slip concrete paths and pathways across Melbourne — properly based and graded so they drain, don't crack and give safe footing year-round. Book a free on-site quote and we'll give you a fixed price before any work starts.

WHAT WE BUILD

A concrete path is a narrow, pedestrian-rated slab that connects the areas around your home — side access, garden runs, front entry, or a link between a driveway and a backyard. Because paths carry foot traffic rather than vehicles, they're thinner than a driveway or garage slab, but the fundamentals are the same: a compacted base, the right falls for drainage, and control joints to manage cracking.

Side access paths

— the narrow run down the side of the house; the most common path job.

Garden & connecting paths

— links between lawn, patio, shed and entertaining areas.

Front & entry paths

— the path from the street or driveway to the front door.

Accessible paths

— wider, gently graded paths for prams, wheelchairs and easy access.

PATH FINISHES

The path can match the rest of your concrete or stand on its own:

  • Plain concrete — the practical, cost-effective standard, with a broom finish for grip.
  • Exposed aggregate — a textured, non-slip finish that looks the part and grips underfoot; popular where the path is on show.
  • Coloured — tinted to match a driveway or the home's colours.

WHY MELBOURNE CUSTOMERS CHOOSE US

  • On-site fixed-price quotes — we measure the run and check the falls before we price.
  • Safe footing — non-slip finishes and correct grading so paths don't pond or get slippery.
  • Licensed & insured
  • Workmanship guarantee

HOW WE LAY A PATH

  • Set out & excavate — mark the run, dig to depth, allowing for the base and slab.
  • Base & compaction — lay and compact a crushed-rock base along the path.
  • Formwork & falls — form the edges and set the falls so water runs off, not toward the house.
  • Pour, finish & joints — pour, screed, apply the chosen finish (broom, exposed, coloured), and cut control joints.
  • Cure — cure properly before use.

WHAT DOES A CONCRETE PATH COST IN MELBOURNE?

Path cost depends on length, width, finish and access — a straight side path is simple; a winding garden path or one with tricky access takes longer. Paths are usually priced by the square metre or lineal metre, and our concrete cost guide covers the typical per-square-metre ranges by finish. We give a free on-site fixed-price quote so you know the real number before committing.

Get a free fixed-price quote →

NON-SLIP & DRAINAGE

Two things make or break a path: grip and water. We finish paths with a non-slip texture — a broom finish or exposed aggregate — so they're safe when wet, and we grade them with the correct falls so rainwater runs off rather than pooling or draining toward the house. Getting the falls right at the start is what stops a path becoming a slip hazard or a damp problem later.

AREAS WE SERVICE

We lay exposed aggregate across Melbourne, including Werribee, Point Cook, Tarneit, Hoppers Crossing, Melton, Craigieburn, Cranbourne, Berwick, Pakenham and Frankston.

FAQ

How much does a concrete path cost in Melbourne?


It depends on length, width, finish and access. A straight side path is more affordable than a winding garden path or one with difficult access. We give a free on-site fixed-price quote with the real figure.

Are concrete paths slippery when wet?

Not when finished right. We use a non-slip texture — a broom finish or exposed aggregate — so paths keep their grip in the wet, which matters most for side access and entry paths.

How wide should a path be?

A standard side path is around 900mm–1m wide; paths for prams, wheelchairs or two-way foot traffic are made wider. We’ll recommend a width for how you’ll use it.

How thick does a concrete path need to be?

Paths carry foot traffic, so they’re thinner than driveways — typically around 75–100mm on a compacted base, with reinforcement where the ground or use calls for it.

Do you handle the drainage and falls?

Yes — we grade every path with the correct falls so water runs off and away from the house, which is as important as the concrete itself.

item.title: Concrete Patios & Alfresco Melbourne
item.dc:creator: Admin-iU1Tj
item.content:encoded:
Concrete Patios & Alfresco Areas in Melbourne

Planning an outdoor entertaining area? We build concrete patios and alfresco spaces across Melbourne — from plain broom finishes to exposed aggregate and honed concrete — poured level, properly drained, and finished to flow with your home and garden. Book a free on-site quote and we'll give you a fixed price before any work starts.

WHAT WE BUILD:

A concrete patio is the outdoor living area where you entertain, dine and relax — an alfresco under the roofline, a freestanding entertaining area in the yard, or a courtyard between spaces. Every patio sits on a properly based, reinforced concrete slab, but the patio is defined by its finish and how well it connects to the house and garden. That's where the value is: a patio that looks and feels like an extension of your living space, not just a grey pad.

Alfresco areas

— the covered outdoor room under your home's roofline or a pergola.

Freestanding entertaining areas

— a standalone patio in the yard for dining and BBQs.

Pool-side patios

— non-slip surrounds that tie the pool area together.

Courtyards & connecting areas

— smaller paved spaces linking house, garden and paths.

PATIO FINISHES

The finish is what turns a slab into a patio — and where most of the decision sits:

  • Exposed aggregate — textured, non-slip and premium; the most popular patio finish.
  • Honed / grind-and-seal — a smooth, polished-look finish; well suited to alfresco and covered areas (not driveways, for slip reasons).
  • Coloured — oxide tinted through the mix to match your home or landscaping.
  • Plain broom finish — the practical, cost-effective option with reliable grip.

WHY CUSTOMERS CHOOSE US

  • On-site fixed-price quotes — we look at the space, levels and how it meets the house before we price.
  • Finish-first — we help you choose a finish that suits the area and how you'll use it.
  • Licensed & insured
  • Workmanship guarantee

HOW WE BUILD A PATIO

  • Set out & excavate — mark the area, dig to depth, set levels to meet the house and garden.
  • Base & compaction — compacted crushed-rock base and a vapour barrier under the slab.
  • Formwork, steel & falls — form the edges, lay reinforcement, and set falls so water drains away from the house.
  • Pour & finish — pour, screed level, then apply the chosen finish (exposed, honed, coloured, broom) and cut control joints.
  • Cure & seal — cure properly, then seal decorative finishes to protect and enrich them.

WHAT DOES A CONCRETE PATIO COST IN MELBOURNE?

Patio cost depends on the area, the finish, site access and whether it needs to tie into existing levels or structures — a plain freestanding patio is very different to an exposed aggregate alfresco graded to meet the house. Decorative finishes cost more than plain concrete, and you can see how the finishes compare on price in our concrete cost guide. We give a free on-site fixed-price quote so you know the real number before committing.

Get a free fixed-price quote →

DRAINAGE & INDOOR-OUTDOOR FLOW

A good patio does two things a bad one doesn't: it drains, and it connects. We grade every patio with the correct falls so water runs away from the house rather than pooling or pushing back toward the building. And we set the levels so the patio meets your threshold cleanly — that seamless step from inside to out is what makes an alfresco feel like part of the home instead of an afterthought. Getting levels and falls right at set-out is what separates a patio that works from one that floods or trips people up.

AREAS WE SERVICE

We lay exposed aggregate across Melbourne, including Werribee, Point Cook, Tarneit, Hoppers Crossing, Truganina and More.

FAQ

How much does a concrete patio cost in Melbourne?

It depends on the area, the finish and site access. A plain patio costs less than an exposed aggregate or honed alfresco. We give a free on-site fixed-price quote with the real figure.

What's the best finish for a patio?

Exposed aggregate is the most popular for its non-slip texture and looks. Honed or grind-and-seal suits covered alfresco areas for a smooth, polished look, while a broom or coloured finish is a cost-effective, practical choice. We match the finish to how you’ll use the space.

Can you match the patio to my house or existing concrete?

Yes — coloured concrete and finish choice let us tie the patio into your home’s colours or existing driveway, and we set the levels so it meets your threshold cleanly.

 

Does a patio need drainage?

Yes. We grade every patio with falls so rainwater runs away from the house, which prevents pooling and protects the building — it’s as important as the finish.

Can you build an alfresco under an existing pergola or roofline?

Yes — we work in to existing structures, setting out the slab and levels to suit the covered area and how it connects to the house.

item.title: Concreters in Point Cook
item.dc:creator: Admin-iU1Tj
item.content:encoded:
Concreters Point Cook

Point Cook is one of Melbourne's fastest-growing bayside suburbs, and its estates mean a steady stream of homes needing everything from fresh driveways to full outdoor areas. We handle the concreting side — new driveways and crossovers, exposed aggregate, slabs, paths and patios — built on a properly compacted base so they last. Whether you're finishing a new build in Saltwater Coast or replacing a tired driveway in an older street, we come out, measure the job, and give you a fixed price before any work starts.

Get Your FREE Quote Today Call Us - 03 4427 9541

Our Services

Whatever the pour, we match you with concreters who do it every week.

Concrete Driveways

New driveways, replacements, crossovers

Exposed Aggregate

The premium textured, non-slip finish with real kerb appeal.

Concrete Slabs

Shed, garage, extension and house slabs fitted properly for your needs

Paths & Pathways

Footpaths, side access, garden paths

Patios & Alfresco

Outdoor entertaining areas

Coloured & Decorative

Coloured, stencil, honed finishes

Our Work in Point Cook:

Point Cook's ground conditions, and why they matter

People assume a bayside suburb means sandy soil. Point Cook doesn't — most of it sits on basalt-plain reactive clay, classified H1 to H2 under AS 2870, the same highly reactive ground as the rest of Melbourne's west. Flat terrain, heavy cracking clay that swells when wet and shrinks when dry, and slabs that move with the seasons if they're not built for it.

What is different about Point Cook is the water and the salt. The suburb is threaded with wetland reserves and drainage corridors running in from Point Cook Coastal Park and the Cheetham Wetlands, and the ground close to the bay carries a high salt content. That combination — reactive clay plus poor drainage plus salinity — is hard on concrete. Standing water against a slab drives the moisture swings that crack reactive clay, and salt attacks poorly specified concrete over time.

So on Point Cook jobs the base is the whole game: a compacted crushed-rock sub-base, reinforcement held at the right height on bar chairs, adequate slab thickness, control joints to let the concrete move, and falls set so water runs off rather than pooling. Get that right and the driveway handles the ground it's sitting on.

Concreting for Point Cook's new estates

Point Cook is built around large master-planned estates — Saltwater Coast, Sanctuary Lakes, Alamanda, Boardwalk and Featherbrook among them. That means a lot of brand-new homes needing driveways, slabs and outdoor areas from scratch, and newer builds where owners want a finish that lifts the look — which is why exposed aggregate and coloured concrete are popular here.

Two things worth knowing on estate lots. Several Point Cook estates, including Sanctuary Lakes and Saltwater Coast, have design covenants that govern driveway finishes and materials, so it's worth checking what your estate allows before you choose. And the lot has usually been compacted by the building trades before the driveway stage, so we check the sub-base rather than assuming it's sound.

Being close to Port Phillip Bay, we also see plenty of outdoor entertaining and poolside work — alfresco slabs, paths and pool surrounds.

Council crossovers in Point Cook

One local catch worth knowing if you're planning a decorative driveway. Point Cook sits in the City of Wyndham, and the vehicle crossover — the section between the road and your property boundary — sits on the council road reserve, not your land. It needs consent from Wyndham City Council, and where there's a footpath it has to be plain concrete. So your exposed aggregate or stencil finish runs up the driveway and stops at the boundary. In the estates, the crossover location is often fixed by the endorsed plan too, so there's less freedom to move it than people expect. We've documented the fees, timelines and design rules in our guide to Wyndham Council's vehicle crossing requirements — and we handle the consent as part of the job, so you're not chasing council yourself.

WHY CHOOSE US

On-site fixed-price quotes

We come to you in Point Cook and price the job on site, so the number doesn't move on the day.

Built for reactive clay and salt

Most failed concrete is failed base. On Point Cook's reactive clay and saline ground, we build for the conditions — proper compaction, correct steel height, adequate thickness and falls that move water away from the slab.

We handle the council crossover

A new driveway that meets the road needs Wyndham Council consent before it's poured. We sort the paperwork and build it to spec as part of the job.

Tidy, finished properly

Clean edges, correct falls, and the site left tidy — the job done the way you'd want it on your own home.

People assume a bayside suburb means sandy soil. Point Cook doesn't \u2014 most of it sits on basalt-plain reactive clay, classified H1 to H2<\/strong> under AS 2870, the same highly reactive ground as the rest of Melbourne's west. Flat terrain, heavy cracking clay that swells when wet and shrinks when dry, and slabs that move with the seasons if they're not built for it.<\/p>\n

What is different about Point Cook is the water and the salt. The suburb is threaded with wetland reserves and drainage corridors running in from Point Cook Coastal Park and the Cheetham Wetlands, and the ground close to the bay carries a high salt content<\/strong>. That combination \u2014 reactive clay plus poor drainage plus salinity \u2014 is hard on concrete. Standing water against a slab drives the moisture swings that crack reactive clay, and salt attacks poorly specified concrete over time.<\/p>\n

So on Point Cook jobs the base is the whole game: a compacted crushed-rock sub-base, reinforcement held at the right height on bar chairs, adequate slab thickness, control joints to let the concrete move, and falls set so water runs off rather than pooling. Get that right and the driveway handles the ground it's sitting on.<\/p>","align":"center","typography_typography":"custom","typography_font_family":"Poppins","typography_font_weight":"400","_padding":{"unit":"px","top":"20","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":false},"__globals__":{"text_color":"globals\/colors?id=astglobalcolor2"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":false,"styles":{"e-d874ac7":{"id":"e-d874ac7","label":"local","type":"class","variants":[{"meta":{"breakpoint":"desktop","state":null},"props":{"padding":{"$$type":"dimensions","value":{"block-start":{"$$type":"size","value":{"size":30,"unit":"px"}},"block-end":{"$$type":"size","value":{"size":30,"unit":"px"}}}},"flex-direction":{"$$type":"string","value":"column"}},"custom_css":null}]}},"interactions":[],"editor_settings":[],"version":"0.0"},{"id":"cd68ea4","elType":"e-flexbox","settings":{"classes":{"$$type":"classes","value":["e-cd68ea4-8624452"]}},"elements":[{"id":"ba0cd46","elType":"widget","settings":{"classes":{"$$type":"classes","value":["e-ba0cd46-bc4e72f"]},"title":{"$$type":"html-v3","value":{"content":{"$$type":"string","value":"Concreting for Point Cook's new estates"},"children":[]}},"link":{"$$type":"link","value":{"isTargetBlank":null}}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"e-heading","styles":{"e-ba0cd46-bc4e72f":{"id":"e-ba0cd46-bc4e72f","label":"local","type":"class","variants":[{"meta":{"breakpoint":"desktop","state":null},"props":{"font-family":{"$$type":"font-family","value":"Poppins"},"font-weight":{"$$type":"string","value":"300"},"font-size":{"$$type":"size","value":{"size":30,"unit":"px"}},"text-align":{"$$type":"string","value":"center"}},"custom_css":null}]}},"interactions":[],"editor_settings":[],"version":"0.0"},{"id":"44bd89e","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

Point Cook is built around large master-planned estates \u2014 Saltwater Coast, Sanctuary Lakes, Alamanda, Boardwalk and Featherbrook<\/strong> among them. That means a lot of brand-new homes needing driveways, slabs and outdoor areas from scratch, and newer builds where owners want a finish that lifts the look \u2014 which is why exposed aggregate and coloured concrete are popular here.<\/p>\n

Two things worth knowing on estate lots. Several Point Cook estates, including Sanctuary Lakes and Saltwater Coast, have design covenants<\/strong> that govern driveway finishes and materials, so it's worth checking what your estate allows before you choose. And the lot has usually been compacted by the building trades before the driveway stage, so we check the sub-base rather than assuming it's sound.<\/p>\n

One local catch worth knowing if you're planning a decorative driveway. Point Cook sits in the City of Wyndham, and the vehicle crossover \u2014 the section between the road and your property boundary \u2014 sits on the council road reserve, not your land. It needs consent from Wyndham City Council, and where there's a footpath it has to be plain concrete. So your exposed aggregate or stencil finish runs up the driveway and stops at the boundary. In the estates, the crossover location is often fixed by the endorsed plan too, so there's less freedom to move it than people expect. We've documented the fees, timelines and design rules in our guide to Wyndham Council's vehicle crossing requirements<\/a> \u2014 and we handle the consent as part of the job, so you're not chasing     A new driveway that meets the road needs Wyndham Council consent before it's poured. We sort the paperwork and build it to spec as part of the job.<\/p>\n\n

item.content:encoded:
Get Your Free Concreting Quote​

Tell us about your job and we'll book an on-site measure and give you a fixed price — no obligation, no pressure. Whether it's a driveway, slab, exposed aggregate, path or patio, the quickest way to get an accurate price is to send a few details or give us a call.

[fluentform id="3"]

PREFER TO CALL?

  • Phone: 03 4427 9541— available Mon–Sat 9am-5pm
  • Email: — shaun@apexframe.org
  • Service area: Werribee, Wyndham and across Melbourne

AREAS WE SERVICE

We lay exposed aggregate across Melbourne, including Werribee, Point Cook, Tarneit, Hoppers Crossing, Melton, Craigieburn, Cranbourne, Berwick, Pakenham and Frankston.

FAQ

Is the quote really free?

Yes — quotes are free and there’s no obligation. We measure the job on site and give you a fixed price; whether you go ahead is entirely up to you.

How soon will you get back to me?

We aim to respond as soon as possible but within one business day should be the most realistic timeframe.

What areas do you cover?

Werribee, Wyndham and across Melbourne. If you’re nearby and not sure, just ask.

item.dc:creator: Admin-iU1Tj
item.content:encoded:
Concrete Driveways in Melbourne

Need a new concrete driveway or the old one replaced? We install plain, exposed aggregate, coloured and decorative concrete driveways across Melbourne's west — properly prepped for reactive clay, correctly reinforced, and finished to last. Most cracked driveways out here failed at the base, not the surface, so that's where we spend the time. Book a free on-site quote and we'll give you a fixed price before any work starts.

Get Your FREE Quote Today

Concrete driveway finishes we lay:

Plain concrete driveways

The durable, cost-effective standard. Clean, hard-wearing, low maintenance.

Exposed aggregate

Stone revealed in the surface for a textured, non-slip, high-end finish.

Coloured & stencil

Colour through the mix or stencilled patterns for kerb appeal.

Reinforced & heavy-duty

Extra steel and thickness for caravans, boats or steep access.

Why Driveways Crack in Melbourne's west:

The ground here moves more than most of Melbourne

Melbourne's western suburbs sit on reactive clay — flat volcanic ground classified from Class M up to Class H under AS 2870, the Australian standard for slabs on reactive soils. The higher the class, the more the ground moves.

Wet winters, dry summers, a slab caught in between

Reactive clay swells when it's wet and shrinks when it dries. Across a Melbourne year of wet winters and dry summers, that means the ground under your driveway is constantly rising and falling. A slab that wasn't built to handle that movement gets flexed every season until it cracks. It's why a driveway that would sit flat for decades in sandy soil can crack within a few years out here — the concrete isn't worse, the ground is working against it.

Most cracked driveways failed at the base, not the surface

The mix is rarely the problem. The problem is a slab laid on moving ground without the preparation that lets it cope — which is why we spend the time on the sub-base, the reinforcement height and the drainage rather than rushing to the pour. If you want the full explanation, we've written a guide on why concrete cracks and how the base controls it.

Thickness, reinforcement and what goes under a driveway

A driveway isn't a path with cars on it — it carries vehicle loads over moving ground, and the spec has to match that:

  • Slab thickness. A standard residential driveway is around 100mm. Thinner slabs don't have the strength to bridge ground movement and vehicle loads at the same time.
  • Reinforcement. Steel mesh — commonly SL72 for a residential driveway — held up on bar chairs so it sits within the slab. Mesh lying on the dirt does almost nothing.
  • Heavier loads. Caravans, boats, trucks or steep access get increased thickness and heavier reinforcement, sized at the quote.
  • The sub-base. A compacted crushed-rock base under the slab, so the concrete sits on uniform support instead of soft spots that settle or fill that heaves.
  • Concrete strength. Specified in MPa (typically 20–32 MPa) to suit the job.

We size the thickness, mesh and mix at the on-site quote rather than pouring a generic spec and hoping. If your driveway needs to take a caravan or sits on a slope, it gets built for that.

HOW WE BUILD A DRIVEWAY THAT LASTS

  1. Site prep & excavation — clear the area, set levels, dig to the right depth.
  2. Base & compaction — crushed-rock base, properly compacted so nothing shifts later.
  3. Formwork & steel — form the edges, lay reinforcing mesh or bar sized to the load, held on bar chairs.
  4. Pour & finish — pour, screed level, and apply your chosen finish (broom, exposed, coloured).
  5. Joints & curing — cut control joints to manage shrinkage, then cure properly before use.

Drainage, falls and finished levels

Your driveway decides where the water goes

A driveway is usually the largest hard surface on a property, which makes it the biggest single influence on where your water ends up. Set the falls wrong and it sends rainwater at the house, ponds against the garage threshold, or drains toward a neighbour.

On reactive clay, bad drainage shortens the driveway's life

Out here it matters twice over. Water pooling along a slab edge drives the exact moisture swings that heave and crack the concrete — so poor drainage doesn't just cause damp problems, it shortens the life of the driveway itself.

Setting levels around what's already there

Before we pour, we set out the levels to work with everything the driveway has to meet: the existing garage floor and door threshold, the footpath and crossover height at the street, any paths that join it, and the natural fall of the block. The aim is water running cleanly off and away from the building, with no lip at the garage and no step where the driveway meets the path.

Replacing an old driveway

Why replacement is so common on established streets

A lot of our driveway work is replacement rather than new pours — particularly on the established streets of Werribee and Hoppers Crossing, where original driveways from the 1970s and 80s have cracked, lifted or become trip hazards.

We rebuild the base, not just the slab

Replacement is more than pouring over the top. We break out and remove the old slab, then look at what's underneath — because if the original failed, the base is usually why. Repouring the same way it was done in 1985 just repeats the failure on the same ground. So the base gets rebuilt properly: excavated to depth, compacted crushed rock, reinforcement at the correct height, and falls corrected if the old driveway drained badly.

Matching levels so there's no lip or step

We also match the new slab into what's staying — the garage floor level, the footpath and crossover, and any paths or gates it meets — so there's no lip or awkward step where new meets old. Removal and disposal of the old driveway is quoted with the job, so you get one fixed number rather than a surprise at the end.

Not sure if yours needs replacing or repairing?

If the slab is sound and the cracking is cosmetic, a repair may be enough. If the base has gone, replacing it properly is better value than patching it twice. Our guide on why concrete cracks covers how to tell the difference, or send us a photo.

How big is a typical driveway?

It helps to know roughly what you're dealing with before you get quotes. On the standard estate lots across Melbourne's west — commonly 350m² to 520m² — a single driveway from the crossover to a double garage usually works out around 40m² to 75m². Wider frontages, longer setbacks, extra parking pads or a turning area push it higher.

Because most concreting is priced per square metre, that range is the biggest single factor in your quote. We measure on site rather than estimating from an aerial photo, so the number reflects the actual job.

Concrete, pavers or asphalt?

Worth knowing what you're choosing between before you commit:

  • Concrete — a single continuous slab. Longest-lasting of the three when it's properly based, lowest maintenance, and the widest range of finishes. Cracks are the main failure mode, which is why base prep decides how long it lasts.
  • Pavers — individual units on a bedding layer. Easy to lift and replace a section, and they handle ground movement by shifting rather than cracking — but they settle unevenly over time on reactive clay, and weeds and ants find the joints.
  • Asphalt — cheaper up front and quick to lay, but softer, shorter-lived, and it needs resealing. It also goes soft in Melbourne heat and marks under a car stand or a caravan jockey wheel.

For most driveways on Melbourne's western clay, a properly prepared concrete slab gives the best working life per dollar — but if you want a surface you can lift and reinstate section by section, pavers have a genuine advantage. We'll tell you if concrete isn't the right call for your site.

Sealing and looking after it

Plain concrete doesn't strictly need sealing, but it benefits from it — a sealer resists oil stains, tyre marks and surface wear, and makes the driveway easier to clean. Decorative finishes should be sealed: it protects the surface, deepens the colour, and on exposed aggregate it's what keeps the stone looking rich rather than dull.

After that, maintenance is minimal — a hose-down, and a reseal every few years depending on traffic and sun exposure. We'll tell you what your specific finish needs and roughly when.

AREAS WE SERVICE:

We pour concrete driveways across Melbourne, including Werribee, Point Cook, Tarneit, Hoppers Crossing, Truganina and More.

What does a Concrete Driveway Cost in Melbourne?

Price comes down to size, finish, site access and whether an old driveway needs removing — plain concrete sits at the lower end, exposed aggregate and decorative finishes cost more. Our concrete driveway cost guide sets out real per-square-metre ranges for each finish, so you can budget before you get anyone out. The only accurate number is an on-site measure, which we do free.

Get Your FREE Quote Today

FAQ

How thick should a concrete driveway be?

A standard residential driveway is around 100mm thick with reinforcing mesh. For heavier vehicles like caravans or trucks, we increase the thickness and steel to suit the load.

How long before I can drive on a new concrete driveway?

It’s usually walk-on ready in 24–48 hours and safe for vehicles after about 7 days. Concrete reaches full strength at around 28 days, and cold or wet weather slows curing.

Do I need council approval for a driveway or crossover?

The crossover onto the road sits on council land and needs approval before anyone pours it — the driveway inside your boundary usually doesn’t. Requirements vary by council, and we’ll point you to yours. In Melbourne’s west, start with Wyndham Council’s vehicle crossing requirements.

How long does a concrete driveway last?

A properly laid and cured concrete driveway commonly lasts 30–40 years or more with minimal maintenance — which is why the base prep matters so much.

Do you remove the old driveway?

Yes — we handle demolition and removal of the existing driveway before the new pour. We’ll confirm whether that’s included or quoted separately at the on-site measure.
